karate-js: built-ins called with no or odd arguments answer as V8 does, not with Java text: JSON.stringify() is undefined and drops built-in and host functions (console's members serialized as Java lambda names), JSON.parse coerces its argument to a string (no ClassCastException or index error), encodeURI()/encodeURIComponent() read "undefined"; Object.keys/values/entries/assign/getPrototypeOf and Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty of null or undefined throw "Cannot convert undefined or null to object", Object.create of a non-object throws, Object.prototype.toString.call(null) is [object Null]; Array callbacks and sort comparators, the Promise resolver, number radix/precision, repeat and normalize use V8's text; 'abc'.at() and String.fromCharCode('a') coerce as specified. RegExp: a brace that opens no quantifier is literal outside u-mode (sugar.js's /{([a-z])}/ no longer fails), \p{...} keeps its braces, RegExp(re) answers re (IsRegExp, same constructor) and new RegExp(re) keeps re's flags, invalid flags and patterns are V8-shaped SyntaxErrors without Java's pattern text. An object literal's anonymous function takes its key as name and an argument no longer takes its parameter's (only a default does); generator and async functions carry their toStringTag; import() is the TypeError Node's vm gives. karate-core Expect's a/an is chai's type-detect (an Error is 'error', null 'null'), over the new Terms.toStringTag.
